does this put a margin at the end of the first button and before the next button?

Yes — `:has(+ ._pendo-button)` matches any `._pendo-button` that has another `._pendo-button` as its next sibling, so it selects every button except the last one in a run, and adds the margin after each of those (i.e., between it and the following button).

One caveat on direction: `margin-block-end` is the logical *bottom* margin in the default horizontal writing mode, not the *right/inline-end* margin. So it only creates visible space when buttons wrap onto separate lines (stacked vertically) — it won't separate buttons that sit side-by-side in a row. Note that [card.css](renderers/pendo/src/css/card.css) already applies `gap: var(--instui-component-shared-tokens-spacing-gap-buttons)` on `.pendo-mock-flexbox-row:has(._pendo-button)`, which handles both row- and column-gap for wrapped flex rows — so this `margin-block-end` may be redundant with that gap in the wrapping case.

Each button has an inline `style="...margin: 10px 5px 10px 0px;..."` (and `margin: 10px 5px;`) set directly in the HTML by Pendo. Inline `style` attributes have higher specificity than any external stylesheet rule (regardless of selector complexity), so your `margin-inline-end` in button.css is being overridden by the inline margin — that's why it's not taking effect.

You'll need `!important` to beat the inline style, consistent with the note in [container.css](renderers/pendo/src/css/container.css)'s doc comment about the build adding `!important` to override Pendo's dynamic inline offsets. Let me check whether that's handled at the build level here.

Found it — but it's not really about `:scope` prefixing. The actual DOM has:

```
class="instui-alert _pendo-step-container _pendo-guide-walkthrough_" data-layout="lightboxBlank"
```

This element carries **both** `._pendo-guide-walkthrough_` (the survey marker) **and** `data-layout="lightboxBlank"` (the alert marker). The overlay/survey block's top-level selector only checks:

```css
:is(:scope, [class*="instui"]):is([data-layout="tooltipBlank"], ._pendo-guide-walkthrough_) {
```

That matches on `._pendo-guide-walkthrough_` alone, with no `data-layout` exclusion — so it fires for this lightboxBlank alert too, and stacks the popover's `border`, `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, and margins on `._pendo-step-container-styles` on top of the embedded-alert's own border/box-shadow/radius from the later block. Note the nested survey-only override two blocks down already guards against this overlap with `:not([data-layout="tooltipBlank"], [data-layout="lightboxBlank"])` — the top-level selector is just missing the same guard.
